title: N-nitrosamines in food
summary: European Commission recommends that food businesses and competent authorities in exporting countries should regularly monitor the presence …
update: The European Commission has published a Recommendation that European Union (EU) authorities and food business operators should monitor N-nitrosamines in food. The European Food Safety Authority has identified the presence of these substances in foods as a potential health concern. However, more data is needed, particularly on the presence of N-nitrosamines in processed meats, alcoholic beverages, processed vegetables and cereals, milk and dairy products, and fermented, pickled, and spiced foods. This data will help the EU to identify measures that can reduce this risk.
impacted_products: Cured meats, processed fish, alcoholic beverages. processed vegetables, processed cereals, milk and dairy products, fermented foods, pickled foods, spiced foods
what_changing:
The European Commission is calling on EU Member States, in cooperation with the food industry, to monitor the presence of N-nitrosamines in food (Recommendation 2026/2329 ).

Monitoring of N-nitrosamines, or at least the 10 carcinogenic N-nitrosamines identified by EFSA, is recommended for the following food categories:

cured meat products and processed fish alcoholic beverages processed vegetables and cereals milk and dairy products fermented, pickled, and spiced foods.

Details on the analysis of N-nitrosamines can be found in the Background section below.

Factors that contribute to high N-nitrosamine levels should also be identified, with a view to developing measures that prevent or reduce contamination.

Monitoring results should be submitted to the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) by Member State authorities and the food industry. This should include information on whether nitrates (E251–E252) or nitrites (E249–E250) were used as additives in processed meats and other processed foods.

This Recommendation does not establish new legal maximum levels for N-nitrosamines in food.
why: N-nitrosamines are chemical contaminants that can form during food processing and preparation. EFSA (2023) assessed the risks associated with ten carcinogenic N-nitrosamines (TCNAs) known to occur in food, and concluded that dietary exposure to these substances raises health concerns.
timeline: EU Member States and the food industry should regularly submit monitoring data to EFSA (see the EFSA webpage Data collection: chemical monitoring ).
actions: Food businesses and competent authorities in exporting countries may wish to review processing practices, particularly the use of nitrates and nitrites, and identify conditions that could contribute to N-nitrosamine formation. Following the developments in EU monitoring and risk assessments will help exporters to anticipate potential future regulatory changes.
background: The ten carcinogenic N-nitrosamines (TCNAs) identified by EFSA that are known to occur in food are: nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA), N-nitrosomethylethylamine (NMEA), N-nitrosodiethylamine (NDEA), N-nitrosodipropylamine (NDPA), N-nitrosodibutylamine (NDBA), N-nitrosomethylaniline (NMA), N-nitrososarcosine (NSAR), N-nitrosomorpholine (NMOR), N-nitrosopiperidine (NPIP) and N-nitrosopyrrolidine (NPYR).
resources: EFSA (2023) Risk assessment of N- nitrosamines in food . EFSA Journal, 21(3): 7884.
